**From:** example-market-data-repo-em · **To:** claude-klabauter-em, DoE, example-game-repo

## The ask

Make prior deep-research dives **durable, machine-readable, and targetable to
`{Target, scope, category_id}`**, with per-dive `ran_at` and `source_refs`, emitting
spans that map 1:1 to our `Utterance` type. This is not an abstract "build the corpus" —
it is a concrete read contract, published below, that you can implement or decline
against.

The read contract is landing this session at `market_intel/scoring/corpus_source.py`
in this repo. Everything below is what that file expects to read.

## The four load-bearing properties

1. **Durable** — a prior dive persists across runs and is retrievable without
   re-running it. (DR-048 on your side already shows `notebook_list` returning 58
   persisted notebooks — the substrate exists; what's missing is a read contract and a
   durability guarantee over it.) Durability is a commitment, not just a persistence
   fact, so it needs a named custodian: whichever team/repo replies should say (a) who
   owns retention for this corpus, (b) a retention commitment stated as something
   checkable — not "indefinitely" — and (c) who to contact when a dive goes missing or
   stale. Without a named custodian, "durable" is a property nobody has actually
   committed to.
2. **Targetable** — retrievable by the same addressing axes our slices already use:
   `Target{uid, label}` (`competitor_uid` for peer scope, the subject repo for our own
   scope, `category_id` for market scope), a `topic`/`query` string, and a
   `scope ∈ {subject_repo, peer, market_category}` discriminator — the same
   `MarketScope` vocabulary our emission contract already uses (DR-010 items 1–2).
3. **Machine-readable** — each dive yields typed, cited spans mappable 1:1 to
   `Utterance{text, source_ref, weight?, locus?, platform?}`, carrying a
   factual/punditry `claim_type` as dive-level provenance (not a scoring input).
4. **Provenance- and freshness-bearing** — each dive carries `dive_id`, `ran_at`, and
   `source_refs`, so a consumed span carries honest provenance and staleness is
   visible. `ran_at` is also what lets a later movement-flagging enabler say "this
   target's corpus is stale, trigger a fresh wave" — durability and staleness compose
   through this one field.

## The published shapes — what we read, what you'd emit

```
# market_intel/scoring/corpus_source.py  (this repo's read contract)

CorpusRequest{target: Target, topic: str, scope: str, category_id: str | None, since: datetime | None}
ResearchDive{dive_id: str, ran_at: datetime, source_refs: tuple[str, ...], spans: tuple[CitedSpan, ...]}
CorpusResult{utterances: tuple[Utterance, ...], provenance: tuple[ResearchDive, ...], coverage_scope: list[str], dark: list[str]}
CorpusProvider.fetch(request: CorpusRequest) -> CorpusResult
```

This is read-only and stateless on our side — we read dives, we never write, tag, or
retain them. `coverage_scope`/`dark` are named to match our existing coverage-honesty
fields exactly (no parallel vocabulary), so a corpus read is coverage-honest through
the same fields a fresh run populates.

Where the corpus lives is deliberately out of scope for this reply — `CorpusProvider`
is a structural Protocol specifying what a corpus must provide, never where it is
stored, so whoever holds it implements the provider. That question belongs to the
`/shape` session named below, not to this consult.

## Addressing-axis alignment — one vocabulary, not two

The corpus needs to be targetable by `competitor_uid` / `category_id` / `subject_repo`
— the exact axes our emission contract already uses (DR-010). This is a request to
share one addressing vocabulary with emission, not to stand up a second one. If D
mints its own `dive_id`/addressing scheme, we'd like it to land inside that same
territory rather than adjacent to it — see the `/shape` note below.

## History, stated plainly

On 2026-07-11 claude-klabauter-em proposed enabler D — a deep-research corpus we could consume
instead of re-deriving (`cross-repo/archive/2026-07-11-claude-klabauter-em-competitive-intel-enablement-vision.md`).
We replied "strong yes... Build it," and that reply is ratified on both sides
(`docs/06-claude-klabauter-consumer-boundary.md § Enabler ownership line`; DR-001 §D). Separately,
`docs/06 § Status` records that a DoE-convened C/D/E alignment was owed "before any
build." That alignment never convened, and no `state/cross-repo-commitments/` ledger
row ever tracked the ask — so the enthusiastic yes had nothing behind it to force a
build or a decline. We're stating that as the finding, not as blame: an ask without a
tracked commitment is not really an ask.

## The fallback — this is not a hostage note

We are building the retrofit seam on our side either way. Our in-flight sentiment
slices will route their `Utterance` acquisition through a `CorpusProvider`
indirection, defaulting to the existing live/fresh path. If this contract lands, it's
a wiring swap. If it doesn't, slices 4–5 ship on re-derivation behind the seam, and D
becomes a scheduled retrofit rather than a reopened decision. Nothing here blocks on
your reply — but a reply, even a decline, closes the loop the way silence didn't.

## The second never-convened alignment worth folding in

There's a separate, still-unfulfilled milestone worth naming alongside this: the
2026-07-11 DoE consult on the adjacent "code + internet intel" enabler committed both
sides to a cross-team `/shape` session ratifying **one shared claim-ID / peer-identity
space** before anyone built against it
(`state/goals/2026-07-11-cockpit-can-truly-query-market-intel.md § Dependencies &
Milestones`). That session never convened either. Our `ResearchDive.dive_id` and
`CorpusRequest`'s addressing scheme land inside exactly that territory — whether
`dive_id` should live inside or outside the shared claim-ID space is a call for
whoever runs that session, not decided by us here. One convened session could plausibly
close both gaps — this one and the C/D/E alignment above — at once.

## Status note

This memo is a **draft** in our outbox, awaiting PM relay. Not yet sent.
